Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure: Sudden onset severe left-sided headache; no clear trigger identified.
- Symptom timeline and progression: Awoke 05:30 today with pain; persistent through day; previously experienced less-severe, frontally distributed headaches.
- ENT symptoms: 
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation: Denied  
  • Voice change: Denied  
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia & drooling: Denied  
  • Nasal/ocular: Mild photophobia; no rhinorrhea, lacrimation, conjunctival symptoms  
  • Stridor/noisy breathing & dyspnea: Denied  
  • Facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling: Denied  
  • Ear/neck: No ear pain or hearing change; no neck stiffness or swelling
- Relevant past episodes and treatments: Intermittent headaches in past (less severe, frontal); no prior medical evaluation or hospital visits for headaches.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Current medications: Sertraline (dose/route/frequency not documented); self-administered Paracetamol this morning (dose/route/frequency not documented); no rescue migraine medications or auto-injector.
- Any relevant social context: Lives with partner; work stress, prolonged hours for past 2 months; exercises (running) ~3×/week.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution: None reported.
- Airway/breathing: No stridor or respiratory distress reported.
- Mental status/associated features: Alert; earlier transient dizziness now resolved.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded.
- Presence of another person: Not applicable during consultation.

Assessment:
- Likely primary headache disorder: tension-type vs. migraine. Features supporting migraine include unilateral pain and light sensitivity; features supporting tension headache include work-related stress and history of anxiety. No red-flag ENT/neurologic features elicited (no neck stiffness, fever, focal neurologic deficit, or airway symptoms).

Plan:
- Pharmacologic: Start Ibuprofen per current migraine guidelines (patient advised dose; dose/route/frequency not documented). May continue Paracetamol if needed.
- Lifestyle: 
  • Self-certify and take ~1 week off work to reduce stress.  
  • Ensure ≥7–8 h sleep nightly.  
  • Hydration goal 1.5–2 L non-caffeinated fluids/day.
- Psychosocial: Provided link to local counseling service for stress/anxiety management; encouraged self-referral.
- Follow-up: Telephone/virtual review in 1 week with GP service; advised earlier contact if symptoms persist or worsen.
- Escalation criteria/red flags: Seek urgent care if new/worsening headache pattern, visual disturbance, focal weakness, confusion, vomiting, neck stiffness, fever, or any airway/breathing difficulties.
- Documentation: Summary and headache danger-sign information to be sent to patient.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing expected elements: No vitals, neurological examination, fundoscopy, or ENT examination documented; no headache diary started; no dose/frequency of Sertraline, Paracetamol, or planned Ibuprofen recorded.
● Internal conflicts: None detected.
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; minimal background noise; complete data capture.
